about: One entry per firmware/<board> (tools/tests/test_flasher_safety.py checks). Hints for the Flasher: how to recognise the board and what to tell the person flashing it. The firmware images themselves come from a bundle. "version" (year.month.n) orders this file against the board descriptions the firmware server offers (FWS-032): raise it with every change, and the newer one wins. A board with "offered": false is known but not installed by the Flasher (not_offered says why): it is never chosen, its images are refused, and bundles are not made for it. The rf pins and the clock module's rtc pins, and their other places (rf.places, rtc.places: RF_PLACES and I2C_PLACES), and the Z-Wave radio's places (zwave.places: ZWAVE_PLACES) are the firmware's own (board_desc.c / board_pins.h; the tests compare them). Pad and pin names are as printed on the board. A board without an rtc entry has no connector for a clock module. "connect" is the maker's advice for plugging the board in: the port this computer uses, the power it needs while it is set up, what to try when it doesn't appear (the CrowPanel's: Elecrow's wiki and the V1.1 schematic, where each 5 V input has its own diode).

crowpanel_p4.name: CrowPanel 7"
crowpanel_p4.revision_note: On V1.2 boards IO27 and IO28 are wired to the radio socket instead.
crowpanel_p4.download_mode: The Flasher restarts the panel into its loader through the USB cable. If that fails: hold BOOT, press and release RESET, then release BOOT, and try again.

steps.do: Slide the POWER switch to ON.
steps.why: The computer can't find the panel while it's off.

steps.do: Plug the cable from this computer into the port marked UART0.
Plug a phone charger into the port marked USB2.0.
steps.why: The computer alone can't power the screen, so it may go dark without the charger.

steps.do: Does the panel have its own power supply? Keep it connected.
steps.why: It's safe to use alongside the computer, and you won't need the phone charger.

not_showing.why: The computer can't find the panel while it's off.

not_showing.do: Is the cable in the port marked UART0?
not_showing.why: The port marked USB2.0 is only for power.

connect.before_install: POWER on, a phone charger on the USB2.0 port (or the panel's own 5 V supply): the panel starts with its screen on at the end, which needs more power than a computer's USB port gives.
connect.more_power: Plug its USB2.0 port into a phone charger (5 V, 2 A or more) as well, then switch it off and on with POWER.

module_wires.to: socket pad IO10, or the J7 pin chosen for it
the receiver antenna, or 17.3 cm of wire

wires.note: the CC1101 is a 3.3 V part

wires.to: a 433 MHz antenna, or 17.3 cm of wire

reserved.25: IO25 is the chip's own USB data line, so it is not offered.
reserved.27: IO27 is kept for the clock module's or the Z-Wave radio's own wiring (on V1.2 boards it is the radio socket's serial line).
reserved.28: IO28 is kept for the clock module's or the Z-Wave radio's own wiring (on V1.2 boards it is the radio socket's serial line).

wires.note: the CC1101 is a 3.3 V part

wires.to: a 433 MHz antenna, or 17.3 cm of wire

j7.note: Its five pins stop being wired zone terminals; IO2, IO3 and IO4 remain. Dupont leads of 10 to 15 cm, the antenna away from the board, the display's ribbon and the Zigbee module's antenna.

wires.note: never 5V: the module's pull-ups would lift the connector's lines above 3.3 V

rtc.note: This connector shares the touch screen's wiring: keep the module inside the case beside it, on 10 to 20 cm of lead away from siren and mains wires, or a fault on it can freeze the touch screen. Match the wires to the printed labels, not their colours.

j7.note: Its own I2C controller: nothing on it can reach the touch screen, and no wired zone is lost. V1.1 boards only: V1.2 boards carry the radio socket's serial line on these two pins.

rtc.cell: A CR2032 coin cell keeps the time through power cuts. Many DS3231 boards (the ZS-042) try to charge it: with a CR2032 remove the charging diode or its resistor, or fit a rechargeable LIR2032.

zigbee.name: ESP32-H2 module
zigbee.note: Elecrow's module made to plug into the socket on top of the board. It takes every pad of the socket, so a 433 MHz receiver goes on J7 while it is there. The panel uses it for Zigbee sensors, and it needs its radio software first: the Flasher installs it.

zwave.name: Zooz ZAC93
zwave.note: The ZAC93 is made for a Raspberry Pi's header: its positions are numbered as a Pi's, 1 to 10. Before wiring, check with a meter on the unpowered radio that positions 1 and 6 are its supply and ground. Its optional reset line (position 7, boards etched Version 2.0) is set on the console: `zwave reset-pin`.

wires.to: socket pad IO53, the panel's TX
socket pad IO54, the panel's RX

crowpanel_10.name: CrowPanel 10.1"

e32r40t.name: E32R40T 4"
e32r40t.not_offered: The 4-inch E32R40T panel is not finished yet, so the Flasher does not install RoboAlarms on it.
e32r40t.download_mode: The Flasher restarts the board into its loader through the USB cable. If that fails: hold BOOT, press and release RESET (EN), then release BOOT, and try again.

cc1101.where: SPI header (the SD card's bus), data on IO35
